result.summary:
Read the full design doc (lib/letflow/design/iss0398-walk-to-gateway-fix.md, all 3 iterations) and the full existing test file (12 tests: AC1-AC6 original + 6 ISS-0398 tests). Found ONE genuine gap: design doc §2.4b explicitly instructs 'TEST-DESIGNER should assert both fixtures' full result tuples are equal, not just that each independently succeeds' for cyclic_escape_graph/0 vs. cyclic_escape_graph_reversed_edges/0 -- the as-written test checked each fixture's own JoinCounter against its own branch_ids and checked 'B' was present in each fixture's own token list, but never compared fixture-A's outcome directly against fixture-B's. Confirmed via reading dispatch_parallel_split/4 (transition.ex:748-798) that a literal full-InstanceState equality would be a FALSE requirement (branch_id/token_id assignment is positional in edges_out, so reversing edge order legitimately swaps which node 't1/0'/'t1/1' land on) -- the actual order-invariant quantity is the JoinCounter itself (join_node_id, origin_token_id, expected_from_branches, received/cancelled sets), since branch_ids is computed purely from length(edges_out) and the parent token_id, independent of edge targets. FIX APPLIED: added `assert Enum.sort(branch_ids_a) == Enum.sort(branch_ids_b)` and `assert counter_a == counter_b` to the cyclic_escape_graph describe block, with an explanatory comment (not a restatement). This is the literal cross-order agreement check the design doc calls for and closes the only real gap found.

EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED (not just reasoned about) that diamond_chain_graph(40) is a genuine complexity regression guard and that the new cross-order assertion is genuinely discriminating, by reverting lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex to each of this run's 3 prior code states and re-running the suite, then restoring (confirmed byte-identical via git diff --stat showing no output each time):
1. Pre-ISS-0398 baseline (commit 8cc047123fc89b3b1fae42e222f0bd381c7cdd3e, unbroadened walk_to_gateway/3): 9/12 passed -- the 3 tests requiring the broadening itself failed as expected (right: {:error, {:no_matching_join_found, "split"}}).
2. Iteration 1 (commit 5691a6a2, broadened but unmemoized -- the exponential-blowup defect SECURITY-REVIEWER found): 10/12 passed. diamond_chain_graph(40)'s test did NOT merely run slow -- it hit ExUnit's 60-second default timeout and was killed outright (** (ExUnit.TimeoutError) test timed out after 60000ms, stacktrace showing deep recursive Enum.map/Enum.filter nesting in collect_leaf_gateways/3). cyclic_escape_graph/0's test also failed (right: {:error, {:no_matching_join_found, "split"}}) -- iteration 1 has no cross-path memoization at all, so it cannot resolve the cyclic case either. This is decisive, unambiguous proof k=40 is a real guard, not a borderline value that happens to still pass fast.
3. Shipped fix (commit 9968fa3b, this branch's HEAD): 12/12 passed, 0.4-0.5s.
I did not separately test iteration 2 (the plain node-keyed memo, 9968fa3b^) in isolation since iteration 1's revert already demonstrates cyclic_escape_graph/0 catching a cross-order defect and the design doc's own §2.4b trace (independently re-read and verified consistent) already documents iteration 2's specific memo['GW'] divergence; the pre-ISS-0398 and iteration-1 reverts were judged sufficient empirical proof for this pass's scope.

Confirmed all other new test cases (branch_with_exclusive_gateway_graph/0's positive/negative pair, pure_cycle_no_escape_graph/0) have meaningful, non-vacuous assertions matching design doc §4's exact specification -- each asserts a specific {:ok,...}/{:error,...} outcome plus JoinCounter/token-placement shape, not merely 'doesn't crash'.

Confirmed test isolation: all fixtures are plain parameterless (or k-parameterized) functions returning fresh %Graph{} literals, no shared mutable state, module stays async: true (pure Transition.transition/3 calls, no Repo/Sandbox), matching three_branch_graph/0's and transition_test.exs's existing conventions.

Final run (mix test test/letflow/engine/parallel_gateway_test.exs, shipped code, this branch's HEAD after the fix): 'Finished in 0.5 seconds (0.5s async, 0.00s sync) / Result: 12 passed'. mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force: clean, zero warnings.

Wrote test/specs/ISS-0398.md documenting the design recap, the gap found and fixed (§2), the empirical k=40 confirmation (§3), the full fail-then-pass proof against all 3 prior code states with real quoted output (§4), the test-case-to-rationale table (§5), and isolation-convention confirmation (§6).

Committed (404ded9a) and pushed to origin/fix/ISS-0398-walk-to-gateway-20260901.
